newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures rise on cash, shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures rise on cash, shortcovering.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures rose at midday Tuesday on shortcovering and steady to higher cash market prices in the the western U.S.
"It's just a lot of shortcovering," said a New York futures broker.
Spot physical prices in the Northwest were supported by cooler-than-normal weather and Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) withdrawing next-day peak offers, market sources said.
"It's fairly cool and nasty in the Northwest so there's a little (more) demand up there," said a Houston futures trader.

BPA announced it will continue to offer next-day firm and non-firm power but only during off-peak demand hours. Monday, the federal agency offered to sell limited amount of non-firm peak power at $13.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) for Northwest deliveries and $14.00 for California-Oregon border (COB).
Day-ahead power prices in the Southwest were buoyant by air-conditioning demand in southern Arizona and New Mexico, traders said.

Next-day electricity prices for peak, firm delivery at COB firmed to $17.25-18.00 from Monday's $15.75-16.50, and those at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard in Arizona jumped to $19.00-19.50 from $16.50-17.00.
AT 1243 EDT, June COB futures were up 55 cents at $13.85 a MWh and July COB climbed 57 cents to $16.20.
June PV futures were up 42 cents at $18.70 a MWh, while July PV notched up 15 cents to $22.95.

In the Northwest, temperatures would stay four to eight degrees Fahrenheit below normal through Wednesday and moderate to normal to four degrees below normal Thursday into the weekend. Unstable atmospheric conditions could bring chance of rain along the coast and in the mountains.
In the Southwest, dry and mild weather would settle over the southern part of the region for the rest of the week with readings averaging three to five degrees F above normal.
Cloudy skies and slightly cooler-than-normal weather were predicted for Utah, Colorado and northern California.
As of 1210 EDT, NYMEX estimated 112 COB and 81 PV contracts were sold.
